note: After passing, return to the right lane only when you can see the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and there is sufficient space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes going your direction, you should:
options: a:Always turn into the farthest lane from your approach.,b:Turn into any lane and then change immediately.,c:Turn into the middle lane regardless of your approach lane.,d:Turn into the lane closest to the lane you came from.
note: Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane and do not change lanes while turning.

question: Two solid white lines painted across a lane denote a crosswalk. What must drivers do when pedestrians are in the crosswalk?
options: a:Drivers may proceed if no vehicle is coming.,b:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in the crosswalk.,c:Assume pedestrians must yield to vehicles
note: Pedestrians in a marked crosswalk have the right-of-way; drivers must stop and allow them to cross safely.

question: When meeting a school bus stopped with red lights flashing, drivers from either direction must:
options: a:Pass if there is a median between you and the bus.,b:Stop at least 30 feet away and not proceed until the flashing red lights are off.,c:Slow down and pass cautiously.,d:Proceed if no children are visible.
note: Drivers in both directions must stop at least 30 feet from a stopped school bus with flashing red lights; do not pass until lights are off and bus resumes motion.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?
options: a:Nothing significant occurs.,b:Alcohol cures common medication side effects.,c:The medicine always blocks alcohol's effects.,d:The combination can multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.
note: Alcohol combined with other drugs can increase impairment beyond that caused by either substance alone.

question: What effect can eating or drinking while driving have?
options: a:Drivers make no driving errors.,b:Drivers have trouble maintaining slow speeds.,c:It increases driver distraction and may reduce lane control
note: Eating, drinking, or similar tasks take your hands and eyes off driving and increase the chance of lane deviation and other driving errors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed only.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Check mirrors and blind spots and signal your lane change.
note: Signal your intention, check rearview and side mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes.

question: Which of the following is true about passing motorcycles?
options: a:The driver of a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.,b:It is acceptable to pass a motorcycle within the same lane.,c:Drivers of other vehicles may follow motorcycles closely.,d:Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a lane and must be passed by changing lanes entirely.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane width; change lanes completely before passing and ensure you are entirely in the left lane when passing on the left.

question: Which feature is sometimes used on highways to channel drivers into the correct turning lanes?
options: a:White lines on the side of the road,b:Flashing yellow lights,c:Flashing red lights
note: Some highways use lane-control or turning arrow signals, such as flashing yellow lights or arrow indications, to show which lanes are for turning.

question: When changing lanes you should not:
options: a:Fail to check for other drivers who may be moving into the same lane.,b:Check your mirrors and signal.,c:Look over your shoulder to confirm the blind spot is clear.,d:Ensure there is enough space to complete the lane change.
note: Never change lanes without checking for other drivers, including blind spots and mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you signal while changing lanes or turning?
options: a:Always signal your intentions, even when no other traffic is visible.,b:Only if there is visible traffic present.,c:Only when driving at night
note: You must signal every time you change lanes or turn so other road users can anticipate your actions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended downward, what does this signal mean?
options: a:The driver is signaling for help.,b:The driver intends to turn right.,c:The driver intends to stop or slow.,d:The driver intends to turn left.
note: An extended left arm with the hand pointing down signals the driver plans to stop or slow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when driving to an unfamiliar destination?
options: a:Plan your route in advance and consult a map or directions.,b:Rely solely on road signs to guide you,c:Drive with only a general idea of the destination,d:Stop frequently to ask random pedestrians
note: Planning ahead helps avoid last-minute maneuvers and reduces distraction when driving in unfamiliar areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp must:
options: a:Enter at any speed without checking traffic.,b:Expect drivers on the interstate to stop for them.,c:Yield to drivers already on the interstate and merge safely when possible.,d:Force their way into traffic.
note: Yield to vehicles already on the highway and use the acceleration lane to merge safely.

question: Which factor does stopping distance not depend on?
options: a:Your own reaction time.,b:The time of day.,c:The condition of your vehicle's brakes
note: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, speed, vehicle weight, tire and brake condition, roadway conditions, and visibility — not the time of day itself.

question: Which behavior is a common indicator that a driver may be intoxicated?
options: a:Weaving between lanes or making sudden stops.,b:Driving slightly below the speed of traffic only.,c:Using turn signals appropriately.,d:Keeping a constant lane position
note: Signs of impaired driving include weaving, erratic speed changes, jerking motions, and sudden stops; such behaviors indicate danger to others.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do first?
options: a:Overcorrect the steering.,b:Turn your steering wheel into traffic.,c:Steer in the direction of the skid
note: If a skid begins, remain calm and steer in the direction of the skid to regain control; avoid abrupt braking or overcorrection.

question: A red traffic signal light requires you to:
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection.,b:Stop at the stop line.,c:Stop before entering any crosswalk.
note: A steady red light requires you to stop at the stop line; if none, stop before entering the crosswalk or intersection.

question: How is distracted driving best characterized?
options: a:Extremely risky behavior that increases the chance of a crash.,b:Very uncommon and of little concern.,c:Only a problem for new drivers.,d:Safe when done occasionally.
note: Distracted driving diverts attention from the driving task and greatly raises the risk of collisions.

question: What may occur when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects of both may be increased.,b:Nothing will change.,c:All effects will be reduced.,d:You will sober up faster.
note: Alcohol plus other drugs can enhance impairment and increase the risk of serious effects on driving ability.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Look into the corresponding side mirror.,b:Look into the rearview mirror,c:Quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
note: To check your blind spot, look over your shoulder toward the lane you plan to enter to ensure no vehicle is hidden from the mirrors.

question: A pennant-shaped traffic sign is used to indicate which situation?
options: a:School zones,b:Regulatory instructions,c:Speed limits,d:No passing zones
note: Pennant-shaped (sideways triangle) signs mark the start of a no passing zone; text may also appear to confirm the message.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a busy freeway, how should you merge into traffic?
options: a:Use your mirrors and check blind spots, and adjust speed in the acceleration lane to match freeway traffic.,b:Yield to traffic only after stopping on the ramp.,c:Always stop at the end of the ramp before merging.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match freeway speed, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway before merging.

question: A bicyclist who disobeys traffic laws:
options: a:May be ticketed like a motor vehicle operator.,b:Is exempt from citations.,c:Will always be stopped and warned by police.,d:Cannot cause liability in an accident.
note: Bicyclists have the same rights and duties as motor vehicle drivers and can be ticketed for violations.

question: \Highway hypnosis\" is caused by:"
options: a:Frequent rest stops.,b:Too much sleep the night before your trip.,c:Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
note: Staring straight ahead for long stretches without actively scanning can cause a trance-like state called highway hypnosis; take breaks and stay alert.

question: Besides turn signals, what may communicate your intention to turn to other motorists?
options: a:Turning your wheels sharply in advance.,b:Braking hard several times,c:Flashing your headlights repeatedly.,d:Your vehicle position and eye contact.
note: Vehicle position and making eye contact can supplement proper signaling to indicate your intended direction to other road users.

question: If a flagger is controlling traffic in a construction zone, you must:
options: a:Assume the flagger is not supposed to be directing traffic.,b:Copy what surrounding traffic does regardless of the flagger's signals.,c:Follow the flagger's directions.
note: Follow the instructions of flaggers in work zones; failing to do so is illegal and dangerous for workers and other road users.

question: If your wheels slip off the edge of the pavement while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Slam on the brakes and stop,b:Jerk the steering wheel sharply to return to the road immediately.,c:Speed up and bounce back onto the pavement quickly,d:Slow down gradually while driving with wheels off the pavement, then steer back when safe.
note: Keep control by slowing gently with the wheels off the pavement, then when safe steer back on gradually—do not yank the wheel.

question: When you hear a siren behind you on the roadway, what must you do?
options: a:Pull over to the right and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.,b:Stop immediately where you are regardless of conditions.,c:Speed up to get out of the way.,d:Turn into the left lane and continue.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches from behind with sirens or lights, you should safely pull over to the right and stop to clear the way.

question: Drivers who have been drinking before driving generally:
options: a:Lack sufficient control over their bodies and judgment to drive safely.,b:Are always aware of the risks they are taking,c:Become better drivers because they are more careful,d:Are unaffected after a single drink
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, reaction time, and motor control; even small amounts can reduce driving ability.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where you and a vehicle to your right arrive at the same time, you should:
options: a:Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.,b:Speed up and get through the intersection.,c:Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
note: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your right; proceed only when it is safe.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?
options: a:Never—mirrors are enough.,b:Only when parking.,c:Only when backing up.,d:When changing lanes, turning, or pulling toward or away from a curb.
note: Always glance over your shoulder to check blind spots before changing your vehicle’s position.

question: How should you negotiate turns on slick roads?
options: a:Change lanes quickly before the turn.,b:Accelerate quickly through the turn.,c:Take turns more slowly than usual
note: Reduce speed before entering curves and turns when roads are slippery; avoid sudden acceleration or steering inputs.

question: Driving while distracted by other activities generally:
options: a:Is never dangerous.,b:Usually causes the driver to react more slowly to hazards.,c:Usually causes the driver to drive faster.
note: Distracted driving slows reaction times and reduces the driver's ability to respond to hazards; it is unsafe.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim high beams, where should you look to reduce glare?
options: a:Toward the left side of the road.,b:At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.,c:Toward the right side of the road.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded by oncoming high beams while keeping enough vision to stay in your lane.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing without gates or flashing lights, how should you act?
options: a:Cross quickly without looking,b:Change gears while on the tracks to prevent stalling,c:Always stop before crossing regardless of visibility.,d:Be prepared to yield to any train and ensure your entire vehicle can clear the tracks.
note: At ungated crossings, look both ways and only cross when you can clear the tracks; avoid stopping or shifting gears on the tracks.

question: A traffic light showing a green arrow and a red light means you may:
options: a:Drive only if you proceed straight ahead.,b:Drive only in the direction of the green arrow.,c:Wait for a solid green light before moving in any direction.
note: A green arrow with a red light allows movement only in the direction the arrow points, provided the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to change lanes, which of the following is important?
options: a:Signal your intentions ahead of the lane change.,b:Check your blind spot.,c:Make sure the lane is clear before entering
note: Always signal early, check mirrors and blind spots, and confirm the lane is clear before changing lanes.

question: On a highway divided by two solid yellow lines, when may you cross them?
options: a:Never under any circumstance,b:To overtake bicycles only,c:To pass another vehicle if no oncoming traffic is visible,d:Only to make a left turn into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing; crossing is allowed only to make left turns into private roads, driveways, or alleys where permitted.

question: If you are taking an over-the-counter medication, you should:
options: a:Read the labels on the drug before driving.,b:Continue to drive regardless of any warning labels.,c:Drink alcohol instead.
note: Many non-prescription medicines can affect driving. Read labels and, if unsure, ask a doctor or pharmacist about driving while taking them.

question: An “End school zone” sign means:
options: a:Children are present all day.,b:You must reduce speed to 20 mph.,c:The reduced school-zone speed limit has ended.,d:The school zone speed begins here.
note: The “End school zone” sign indicates the end of a reduced speed school zone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you pass another vehicle?
options: a:When your lane is next to a solid yellow line and the other lane is clear ahead.,b:In a curve or on a hill if you think there is little chance of oncoming traffic.,c:By using the shoulder of the highway.
note: You may only pass where it is legal and safe; never pass on hills or curves where visibility is limited or by driving on the shoulder.

question: You may pass another vehicle if the line dividing your lane from the lane you wish to enter is a:
options: a:Broken white line.,b:Double solid yellow line.,c:Solid yellow line.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to pass when safe.

question: At a light rail crossing, you should always:
options: a:Look both ways before crossing tracks and obey signals.,b:Drive around lowered gates if you can.,c:Assume trains will stop for vehicles.,d:Cross without stopping if no train is visible.
note: Never drive around lowered gates; always look both ways and obey crossing signals and signs.

question: When are you allowed to cross double solid yellow center lines?
options: a:To pass a slow-moving vehicle at any time.,b:To pass another car when there is no oncoming traffic.,c:To change lanes quickly,d:To turn left into or out of a driveway or to make a permitted left turn.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing and lane changes except to turn left to enter or exit a roadway, driveway, or where U-turns are allowed.

question: A double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road means:
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and indicate no passing in either direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an intersection and the light turns solid yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Stop before entering if you can do so safely; otherwise proceed through cautiously.,b:Speed up to beat the red.,c:Treat it as a green and go normally,d:Immediately stop in the middle of the intersection
note: A solid yellow warns the light will turn red soon; stop safely if possible, otherwise proceed through the intersection carefully.

question: Round traffic signs typically warn of:
options: a:School zones.,b:Upcoming railroad crossings.,c:No passing zones.
note: Round signs are used to warn drivers of railroad crossings ahead; exercise extra caution when you see them.

question: You must yield to an emergency vehicle when:
options: a:You see flashing lights or hear a siren.,b:Only if it is following traffic lawfully.,c:Never — emergency vehicles yield to you.,d:Only during daytime hours.
note: Yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights by pulling over and stopping when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, where should you stop?
options: a:Stop immediately where you are.,b:Stop on the right side of the roadway.,c:Stop and wait only until the light turns green.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles using lights or sirens by pulling to the right edge of the road and stopping until they have passed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, you should:
options: a:Go to the next exit.,b:Make a U-turn through the median.,c:Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
note: If you miss an exit, continue to the next exit — do not stop, back up, or make an unsafe turn on the freeway.

question: What does a diamond-shaped traffic sign generally indicate?
options: a:An interstate route marker.,b:A school crossing only.,c:A regulatory prohibition,d:Warning of road hazards or special conditions ahead.
note: Diamond-shaped signs (usually yellow) warn drivers of hazardous locations or areas requiring special caution; in work zones they are often orange.

question: Which condition increases your vehicle's stopping distance?
options: a:When driving at night.,b:On a wet or icy road.,c:On paved highways.,d:When using cruise control.
note: Stopping distances increase on wet, icy, loose gravel, or otherwise slippery surfaces.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you proceed through an intersection that has a stop sign but no marked stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:Only if you have to stop at least 20 feet away,b:After honking to alert others,c:After coming to a complete stop at a point where you can see traffic and it is safe to go.,d:After slowing slightly to check for traffic but not stopping.
note: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection at a point where you can see approaching traffic and proceed when safe.

question: If involved in an accident, a driver must:
options: a:Stop at or near the scene, move vehicles out of traffic if possible, and turn off ignitions of wrecked vehicles.,b:Leave immediately and report later.,c:Refuse to provide any information.,d:Continue driving if damage is minor.
note: Stop at or near the scene, move vehicles out of the way if safe, and turn off ignitions of wrecked vehicles to reduce hazards.

question: How can you reduce the chance of hydroplaning?
options: a:Drive faster to get through wet areas quickly.,b:Drive more slowly in wet conditions.,c:Follow closely behind the vehicle ahead.,d:Shift to neutral when water is deep.
note: Hydroplaning is caused by driving too fast on wet surfaces; reducing speed helps maintain tire contact with the road.

question: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are divided by which color lines?
options: a:White,b:Black,c:Yellow,d:Red
note: Yellow lines separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions; white lines separate lanes moving the same direction.

question: To ensure your physical condition does not make driving unsafe, you should:
options: a:Keep physically fit and have regular physical examinations.,b:Know the effect of any medicine on your driving ability.,c:Drive within your physical limitations.,d:All of the above
note: Be aware of health, medications, and physical limitations; take steps to ensure you are fit to drive safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may drive left of a highway's centerline:
options: a:When overtaking and passing another vehicle, if passing is permitted.,b:When you have 500 feet of clear road ahead and to the rear.,c:When the shoulder of the road is rough and the ditch is deep.
note: You may cross the centerline to overtake and pass when it is legal to do so and the way is clear; do not cross solid yellow lines or in no-passing zones.

question: On slippery roads, what should you do to improve safety?
options: a:Drive as you would on dry roads.,b:Use alternate routes.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: Increase following distance on slippery surfaces because stopping distances are longer and traction is reduced.

question: Which practice can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Driving as close as possible to the vehicle ahead.,b:Constantly switching lanes to gain advantage.,c:Honking frequently to assert yourself.,d:Allowing extra travel time and using proper signals.
note: Allowing extra time, signaling properly, and obeying speed limits help reduce road rage incidents.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left, drivers should:
options: a:Accelerate into the turn to clear traffic.,b:Always stop in the middle of the intersection.,c:Turn from any lane regardless of markings.,d:Signal several seconds in advance, check mirrors, slow gradually, and watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
note: Signal 3–5 seconds early, slow down, check mirrors and the path, and yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic before turning left.

question: If you are involved in a serious motor vehicle crash, what is the first action you must take?
options: a:Determine if anyone is injured.,b:Call the police.,c:Stop your vehicle
note: If involved in a crash, stop your vehicle, move it out of traffic if possible, check for injuries, call emergency services when needed, and report the crash when required by law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where should you reduce speed when exiting a highway?
options: a:Once you have moved into the exit lane and are on the deceleration ramp.,b:On the main highway just before the exit lane.,c:Only after you see a toll booth,d:After you pass the exit sign
note: Do not slow on the mainline; move into the exit lane then slow on the deceleration lane to avoid impeding through traffic.

question: The best ways to avoid hydroplaning include:
options: a:Keep your tires properly maintained.,b:Watch out for standing water or puddles.,c:Slow down when roads are wet.,d:All of the above
note: Maintain tire tread and pressure, reduce speed on wet roads, and avoid standing water to lower hydroplaning risk.

question: Which is the leading cause of fatalities on Montana roads?
options: a:Poor or unkempt roads,b:Inclement weather/driving conditions,c:Drunk drivers
note: Alcohol-impaired driving is a leading cause of traffic deaths in Montana and nationally; it contributes to a large share of fatalities and injuries.

question: How should you respond to a flashing red traffic light at an intersection?
options: a:Stop only if other cars are approaching.,b:Come to a full stop and proceed when safe.,c:Slow down and proceed without stopping
note: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop, yield the right-of-way, and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do before making a left turn?
options: a:Sound your horn loudly,b:Swing to the right then back left,c:Speed up to clear the turn quickly,d:Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: Before turning left you must yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians and only turn when it is safe.

question: When merging onto a freeway, what is the best practice?
options: a:Proceed slowly while waiting for an opening.,b:Use the on-ramp to accelerate to freeway speed and blend with traffic.,c:Turn on your hazard lights until fully merged
note: Use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of freeway traffic so you can safely merge without disrupting the flow of vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than:
options: a:The maximum speed limit at all times.,b:Any speed that keeps up with traffic flow.,c:Twice the posted speed limit.,d:A speed that is reasonable and prudent for conditions even if below the posted maximum.
note: You must drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent for the conditions, not merely the posted maximum speed.

question: What does a solid white centerline on a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,c:Lanes moving in the same direction and drivers may pass when safe
note: Solid white lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction and discourage or prohibit lane changes where marked.

question: A flashing yellow traffic light means:
options: a:Merging traffic,b:Pedestrian crossing,c:Proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to slow down and proceed with caution through the intersection.

question: If you move, you must report your address change to the Driver License Bureau within:
options: a:Two weeks.,b:10 days.,c:15 days.,d:One month.
note: Notify the Driver License Bureau within 10 days of any change of address to keep your license records current.

question: The effect alcohol has on reflexes and judgment is:
options: a:Most pronounced when consuming hard ciders and mixed drinks.,b:Less pronounced when consuming beer instead of wine.,c:Less pronounced when consuming wine instead of beer.,d:Dependent on how much alcohol is in the bloodstream, not the type of beverage.
note: Impairment depends on blood alcohol concentration; the type of alcoholic drink does not change how alcohol affects reflexes and judgment.

question: To prepare for hazards ahead, you should:
options: a:Stare straight ahead at all times.,b:Continually scan the entire road and all roadsides.,c:Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake pedal.
note: Continuously scan the road ahead and the sides to identify potential hazards early and give yourself time to react.

question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, you should:
options: a:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.,b:Stay in the driver's blind spot.,c:Keep a steady pace.
note: Do not remain in another vehicle’s blind spot; either speed up slightly or fall back so the driver can see you in their mirrors.

question: When approaching a flashing yellow light, you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop completely every time.,c:Turn on your headlights.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: A flashing yellow light warns of a potential hazard; slow and proceed carefully.

question: If you are on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches, you must:
options: a:Drive with your flashers turned on.,b:Speed up and take the nearest exit.,c:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.
note: On a one-way street you should drive to the nearest side and stop to yield to the emergency vehicle.

question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?
options: a:Keep your speed constant once in the exit ramp.,b:Slow down once you move onto the exit ramp.,c:Slow down before entering the exit ramp.
note: Do not begin to slow while on the travel lane; accelerate onto the ramp and then slow once you are on the exit ramp and clear of traffic.

question: When driving in traffic, what is generally the safest approach regarding speed?
options: a:Fluctuate your speed to stay alert.,b:Drive faster than the flow of traffic.,c:Maintain a speed consistent with the flow of traffic and posted limits
note: To reduce collision risk, drive with the normal flow of traffic within the posted speed limits; avoid driving significantly faster or slower than surrounding vehicles.

question: An advisory speed sign attached to a curve warning means you should:
options: a:Ignore the advisory in rainy or icy conditions.,b:Speed up when entering the curve.,c:Reduce speed in poor conditions rather than ignoring the advisory.,d:Always maintain the posted highway limit.
note: Advisory speeds beside curve signs are recommended speeds and should be reduced further in rain, snow, or ice.

question: When entering the roadway from a private road or driveway, what is required of you?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and vehicles already on the roadway.,b:Enter quickly without stopping if the road looks clear.,c:Sound your horn to warn approaching traffic,d:Stop with part of your vehicle on the roadway to alert others
note: When coming from a private road or driveway, you must yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway before entering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an uncontrolled intersection, you should:
options: a:Maintain your speed and proceed.,b:Stop at the intersection, check in all directions, and proceed.,c:Yield to a vehicle approaching from the right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, be prepared to yield to vehicles approaching from your right; slow, cover the brake, and look both ways.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is crossing a single broken white or yellow line not allowed?
options: a:When turning left into a driveway.,b:When doing so would interfere with traffic.,c:When the car in front of you is disabled.
note: You may cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes only if you can do so safely and without interfering with other traffic.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked at the curb, what should you assume?
options: a:That the driver will open the car door as you approach.,b:That the driver will wait for you to pass.,c:That the parked vehicle will roll into the street
note: Approach parked cars cautiously and assume a door or occupant may suddenly enter the roadway; leave extra clearance when passing.

question: Which color lines separate lanes moving in the same direction?
options: a:White,b:Yellow,c:Red
note: White lines (solid or broken) separate lanes moving in the same direction; broken white lines may be crossed to change lanes.

question: What is the purpose of highway pavement markings and other markings?
options: a:They are usually not important.,b:They are only used in construction zones.,c:They provide drivers with information
note: Pavement and highway markings guide lane positioning, passing zones, directions, and warn of upcoming road conditions.

question: When parallel parking between two cars, you should first:
options: a:Turn your wheels to the left.,b:Turn your wheels to the right.,c:Pull up even with the car in front of your desired parking space.
note: After signaling and checking traffic, stop parallel to the vehicle ahead of the space before beginning your back-in maneuver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are turning left onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Either lane,b:The lane closest to your previous lane,c:The right lane
note: When turning onto a one-way street, turn into the lane nearest to the direction you entered from, unless signs indicate otherwise.

question: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) depends on each of the following, except:
options: a:Your body weight.,b:How much you drink.,c:How much time passes between drinks.,d:The type of alcoholic beverage you drink.
note: BAC depends on how much you drink, your body weight, and the time between drinks; the beverage type does not change BAC directly.

question: Worn or bald tires can:
options: a:Increase stopping distance and make turning more difficult.,b:Reduce fuel consumption.,c:Improve traction in wet conditions.,d:Ensure a smoother ride.
note: Tires with inadequate tread increase stopping distances, make steering less effective, and raise the risk of hydroplaning.

question: How should you pass a bicyclist on a two-lane road that has no bicycle lanes?
options: a:Wait until no oncoming traffic, then pass leaving sufficient space.,b:Pass immediately and move back into lane quickly.,c:Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign
note: Pass bicyclists as you would other vehicles, but allow at least 3 feet of clearance (more at higher speeds) and only pass when it is safe.

question: What do pentagonal traffic signs indicate?
options: a:Speed limits,b:School zones,c:No passing zones
note: Pentagonal (five-sided) signs identify school zones and school crossings; watch for children and pedestrians in these areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You plan to turn left but oncoming traffic is heavy. What is the correct course of action?
options: a:Use the next intersection to turn.,b:Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.,c:Enter the center of the intersection and wait for an opening if the light is green
note: If the light is green and you need to prepare for a left turn, you may enter the intersection and wait for a safe gap in oncoming traffic before completing the turn.

question: Before switching on the ignition, what safety routine should you follow?
options: a:Be sure all passengers, including children, have buckled their seat belts.,b:Be sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.,c:Be sure only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts
note: Develop a routine of buckling your safety belt and ensuring all passengers are belted before starting the vehicle.

question: Your blind spot is the area:
options: a:You cannot see without moving your head (not visible in mirrors).,b:Directly behind your vehicle only.,c:You see in your rearview mirror.,d:Inside your vehicle cabin only.
note: Blind spots are areas beside and behind your vehicle that cannot be seen in mirrors without a head turn.

question: When a traffic signal shows a flashing yellow arrow for left turns, drivers:
options: a:Must come to a complete stop before turning.,b:Should merge into the lane indicated by the arrow without yielding.,c:Are prohibited from turning left.,d:May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow arrow allows left turns but you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

question: When preparing to change lanes, you should:
options: a:Signal and immediately move over.,b:Check mirrors, signal, and glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot.,c:Only check your side mirror.,d:Change lanes without signaling if traffic is light.
note: Check side and rearview mirrors, use your signal, and glance over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

question: What is the recommended action when approaching a railroad crossing that has no warning signals?
options: a:Assume no trains will come and cross normally.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,c:Always come to a complete stop at every crossing
note: At an unmarked railroad crossing, slow down, look and listen for approaching trains, and stop if a train is visible or audible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at the same time to an open intersection, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,c:One driver may continue driving without stopping.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: How should drivers behave when encountering a funeral procession?
options: a:Always stop and let the procession pass regardless of traffic laws.,b:Drive quickly through the procession to get ahead,c:Ignore the procession and continue normally,d:Do not drive between vehicles in the procession unless authorized by an officer.
note: State law requires drivers and pedestrians to yield to funeral processions; do not enter intersections that would cross their path unless authorized.

question: Which types of drugs can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Cold remedies and some over-the-counter medications,b:Marijuana,c:All of the above
note: Many substances, including illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medications, can impair driving ability and make it illegal to drive.

question: The most common color of warning signs is:
options: a:Yellow.,b:Red.,c:Green.,d:Blue.
note: Most warning signs are yellow with black markings to warn of unexpected conditions.

question: Which distraction significantly raises the risk of a crash while driving?
options: a:Using a cell phone,b:Listening to the radio calmly,c:Adjusting the seatbelt briefly,d:Wearing sunglasses
note: Using a cell phone is a major distraction and increases crash risk; any device that diverts attention reduces safety.

question: When a traffic signal shows a steady yellow arrow for a turn, drivers should:
options: a:Stop if it is safe to do so because a red arrow is coming.,b:Turn immediately without yielding.,c:Treat it like a flashing yellow arrow.,d:Increase speed to clear the intersection.
note: A steady yellow arrow indicates the protected-turn phase is ending and a red arrow will follow; stop if safe to do so.

question: What should you do to be safe when crossing railroad tracks?
options: a:Look both ways only if flashing lights are active.,b:Listen, look both ways, and then proceed if it is safe.,c:Cross quickly when a train is approaching
note: Always look and listen for approaching trains from either direction and obey any warnings; never proceed until you are certain the tracks are clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit sign shows:
options: a:Only a recommended driving speed.,b:The exact speed at which you must travel to avoid a ticket.,c:The maximum safe driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions.
note: A speed limit indicates the maximum legal speed on that stretch of road under ideal conditions; you may need to drive slower when conditions require.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering a public road from a driveway or private road should:
options: a:Force their way into traffic.,b:Yield to drivers already on the public road.,c:Assume they have the right-of-way.
note: Yield to traffic already on the public road and merge only when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you on a two-lane, two-way road, you should:
options: a:Decrease your speed.,b:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.,c:Not let the other cars pass your vehicle.
note: If you are impeding traffic, pull off the roadway at the first safe opportunity to let vehicles pass.

question: Why should drivers be especially alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They follow completely different traffic laws.,b:They always have the right-of-way.,c:They are required to ride on sidewalks.,d:They can be more difficult to see and judge in traffic than larger vehicles.
note: Smaller road users are harder to spot and their speed and distance can be difficult to judge, so drivers must watch carefully.

question: Which of the following is true regarding seat belts and child restraints?
options: a:Seat belts are unnecessary for rear passengers,b:Always ensure passengers use seat belts or proper child restraints; never place a rear-facing infant seat in a front seat with an active airbag.,c:Child restraints are optional for short trips,d:You can place an infant in the front seat if the airbags are off.
note: Seat belts and child restraints greatly reduce injury risk; children 12 and under should ride in a rear seat. Never put a rear-facing infant seat where an active passenger airbag could strike it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When waiting in the intersection to make a left turn, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Signal and keep your wheels straight,b:Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left,c:Flash your headlights to warn other drivers
note: Signal before turning and keep your wheels straight while waiting; if struck from behind, you will be less likely to be pushed into oncoming traffic.

question: Which trait describes a good defensive driver?
options: a:Stays at the speed limit even under hazardous conditions.,b:Avoids looking at mirrors to focus ahead,c:Always follows closely to control traffic flow,d:Anticipates and watches for the actions of other drivers.
note: A defensive driver anticipates other drivers' actions and prepares to react, reducing collision risk.

question: When is it appropriate to sound your horn?
options: a:If you lose control of your vehicle and need to warn others.,b:When you want to pass another car for speed,c:To express frustration at another driver,d:When approaching a green light
note: Use your horn to warn others of immediate danger (e.g., loss of control); avoid using it for aggression or routine actions.

question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left, where should you glance?
options: a:Over your right shoulder,b:Over your left shoulder,c:At your side mirror only,d:At your rearview mirror only
note: Glance over your left shoulder in the direction you want to move to check blind spots not covered by mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection controlled by a yield sign, you must:
options: a:Always come to a complete stop.,b:Yield the right-of-way to traffic in the intersection or roadway you are entering.,c:Only yield to traffic coming from the right.,d:Proceed without slowing if the way looks clear.
note: A yield sign requires you to slow down and yield to traffic and pedestrians in the roadway you are entering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To enter a freeway safely you should:
options: a:Signal, yield to existing traffic, and enter at the same speed that traffic is moving.,b:Signal and enter the freeway — freeway traffic must yield.,c:Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
note: When merging, match the speed of traffic, use your signal, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway.

question: What color are pavement markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow,b:White,c:Red,d:Blue
note: Yellow pavement markings are used to separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.

question: A steady green arrow on a traffic signal tells drivers they may:
options: a:Ignore other vehicles in the intersection.,b:Proceed straight only.,c:Stop before turning.,d:Turn in the arrow's direction after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.
note: A steady green arrow gives a protected turn; yield to any vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection before turning.

question: Motorcycles on the roadway are entitled to:
options: a:The bicycle lane.,b:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,c:Half the width of a lane.
note: Motorcycles are full-size vehicles for lane purposes and are entitled to the full lane width; do not attempt to share a lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which takes precedence: a steady red light, a police officer's directions, or a stop sign?
options: a:A steady red light,b:A police officer,c:A stop sign
note: Directions from a police officer or authorized traffic controller override signs, signals, and pavement markings; follow their instructions.

question: At night, what is the hardest to see compared to signs and other objects?
options: a:Road signs.,b:Other motorists.,c:Pedestrians.
note: Pedestrians are hardest to see at night; use headlights and be alert for people near or crossing the road.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, you should:
options: a:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.,b:Stop your car on the edge of the road.,c:Slow down and very carefully turn back onto the pavement.
note: If you drop onto the shoulder, slow down without heavy braking and carefully steer back onto the pavement when it is safe to do so.

question: When sharing the road with a large truck, remember trucks generally:
options: a:Require a smaller turning radius than cars.,b:Require less time to pass on a downgrade.,c:Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
note: Due to size and weight, large trucks need much more distance to slow and stop than smaller passenger vehicles.

question: Which actions help you drive safely at night?
options: a:Increase your following distance,b:Ignore your headlights if you are tired,c:Drive faster to get home sooner
note: At night, increase following distance, avoid driving if tired, and ensure headlights and other equipment are working properly.

question: A green arrow on a traffic signal means:
options: a:You may proceed only if the green arrow is accompanied by a circular green light.,b:It has the same meaning as a circular green, but traffic must turn in the direction shown.,c:It is used only on one-way streets.
note: A green arrow indicates you may proceed in the direction of the arrow; it functions like a green light specifically for the indicated movement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On which traffic signal do you have the right-of-way to complete a left turn?
options: a:A solid green light,b:A flashing yellow light,c:A green arrow pointing left
note: A steady green arrow pointing left gives you the right-of-way to turn left while oncoming traffic is required to stop for the turning movement.

question: Alcohol consumption causes which of the following?
options: a:Improved reaction time.,b:Enhanced vision temporarily.,c:Increased ability to judge distance.,d:Loss of concentration, poor coordination, and slower judgment.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair vision, coordination, concentration, and judgment.

question: Stop lines are:
options: a:Painted in curves and on hills.,b:Next to churches and schools.,c:Solid white lines painted across traffic lanes at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
note: Stop lines show the location where drivers must stop for traffic signals or signs and are painted across lanes at intersections and crosswalks.

question: You must use extra caution near a pedestrian holding a white cane because the person is likely:
options: a:To be deaf.,b:To be a police officer.,c:To be blind.
note: When near a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be prepared to stop.

question: As a pedestrian, when should you avoid entering a street or crosswalk?
options: a:When vehicles are approaching and may not have time to stop.,b:Always insist on the right-of-way and step into the crosswalk,c:Enter anytime because drivers must stop,d:Only use crosswalks at night
note: Pedestrians should not step into the roadway when approaching vehicles may not be able to stop; wait until it is safe even if you have the right-of-way.

question: Which type of highway sign warns drivers of potentially hazardous conditions ahead?
options: a:Warning signs,b:Regulatory signs,c:Information signs,d:Guide signs
note: Warning signs alert drivers to hazardous conditions or changes in the roadway; obey them for your safety to avoid accidents.

question: Driving around lowered railroad crossing gates is:
options: a:Allowed when the lights have stopped flashing.,b:Allowed when the train has passed.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: Do not go around lowered gates or ignore warning signals — stop and wait for the proper indication that it is safe to cross.

question: Which statement best describes the driving of drowsy drivers?
options: a:They should drink strong coffee to stay awake.,b:Drowsy drivers may drive so poorly that they appear to be drunk.,c:They can restore alertness by opening a window and turning up the radio
note: Drowsiness impairs driving ability and can make a driver perform similarly to a drunk driver; short-term fixes like opening a window or radio usually are not enough.

question: The best place to keep a space cushion is:
options: a:Only in back of your vehicle.,b:Only in the left and right sides of your vehicle.,c:On all sides of your vehicle.
note: Maintain a cushion of space around your vehicle — front, back, and sides — to give you time to react to hazards.

question: When must headlights be used?
options: a:Only when traffic is very heavy.,b:From one half hour before sunset to one half hour after sunrise.,c:Throughout daylight savings time.
note: Headlights are required from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, and at any time visibility is reduced to less than 500 feet.

question: Why must drivers be especially cautious when driving at night?
options: a:Traffic is denser at night.,b:Visibility is reduced and drivers cannot see as well.,c:Vehicles are faster at night.,d:Road rules change after dark.
note: From half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise (or when people/vehicles are not visible for 500 feet), reduced visibility requires the use of headlights and increased caution.

question: Large trucks differ from passenger vehicles in that they:
options: a:Have smaller blind spots than cars.,b:Always stop more quickly than cars.,c:Are easier to pass at high speeds.,d:Have large blind spots and require more room to maneuver and stop.
note: Trucks have large blind spots and need significantly more space to maneuver and stop than passenger vehicles.

question: A diamond-shaped traffic sign means:
options: a:An indication of a scenic route.,b:A guide sign for services.,c:Warning: existing or possible hazards ahead.,d:A regulatory instruction you must obey.
note: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of potential hazards or changes in the roadway or conditions.

question: Traffic signs that require drivers to obey an instruction are called:
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Information signs.,d:Guide signs.
note: Regulatory signs require compliance (e.g., speed limits, stop, yield); failure to obey may result in penalties.

question: If you feel upset or angry after an incident at work, before driving you should:
options: a:Play the radio loudly so you won’t think about it.,b:Drive fast on the interstate to let off steam.,c:Take a few minutes to cool off before you begin your drive home.
note: Take time to calm down before driving; emotional distress impairs judgment and reaction time.

question: Your brake lights inform other drivers that you are:
options: a:Making a turn.,b:Changing lanes.,c:Slowing down or stopping.
note: Brake lights indicate to drivers behind you that you are slowing or stopping and must be kept in working order.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, the best action is to:
options: a:Get out of the car and go for help.,b:Stay in your car and wait for help.,c:Walk into the road and get the attention of other drivers.
note: Remain in your vehicle, make it visible, run the engine periodically for heat while conserving fuel, and wait for rescuers.

question: If there are two parallel railroad tracks, what should you do after one train passes?
options: a:Always stop before crossing the tracks.,b:It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.,c:Look for another train on the other track before proceeding
note: At multiple-track crossings, wait and check for trains on all tracks; do not cross until you are sure no train is approaching on any track.

question: What should you do when driving in fog?
options: a:Use high beams to improve visibility.,b:Turn on your hazard lights and drive at the speed limit.,c:Turn on your low-beam headlights.
note: Use low beams in fog (not high beams) and reduce speed; when visibility is below 500 feet, headlights must be on.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches, what must you do immediately?
options: a:Turn on your four-way flashers and slow down.,b:Pull to the right and slow down but remain moving.,c:Pull to the right and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with warning devices, you must drive to the right edge of the road and stop until it has passed.

question: After an accident, which of these actions should you take immediately?
options: a:Call the police.,b:Leave the scene if the other driver is at fault.,c:Stop immediately
note: Stop immediately, assist the injured if it is safe, call emergency services when needed, and exchange information; do not leave the scene of a reportable crash.

question: On a road without sidewalks, a pedestrian should walk on:
options: a:The side of the road which has the lightest traffic.,b:The same side of the road on which traffic is moving.,c:The side of the road facing oncoming traffic.
note: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road facing oncoming traffic so they can see and react to approaching vehicles.

question: If your car breaks down on a highway, you should:
options: a:Leave the car in the travel lane and walk for assistance.,b:Sound your horn to alert drivers.,c:Sit in the car and wait for help without signaling.,d:Exit the roadway, use your hazard lights, and make the vehicle visible.
note: Signal before exiting, use hazard flashers, move fully off the road if possible, and make your disabled vehicle visible (e.g., raise the hood).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where should your vehicle be positioned when preparing to make a right turn?
options: a:Near the center of the street.,b:Close to the left side of the street,c:In the left-turn lane,d:As close to the right side of the road as practicable.
note: When turning right, move as far right as practical prior to and during the turn; do not cut across lanes.

question: You want to back out of your driveway and children are playing nearby. What should you do before moving the vehicle?
options: a:Sound your horn to warn the children.,b:Rev the engine so the children will hear your car.,c:Exit the car and walk to the rear to check that the way is clear
note: When children are nearby, get out and check behind your vehicle rather than relying solely on mirrors or a quick glance.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, which additional control should you set?
options: a:Keep the rear tires against the curb and leave in gear.,b:Set it in neutral to prevent strain on the brakes,c:Keep the front tires straight ahead only,d:Set the parking brake and turn the steering wheel away from the curb.
note: Set the parking brake and turn the front wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will rest against the curb if it rolls.

question: Where is it illegal to park your vehicle?
options: a:In a private driveway with owner permission,b:On a hill with the parking brake engaged,c:In a parking lot designated for vehicles,d:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
note: Parking on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane is unlawful; when parking at the curb you must be within 12 inches of the side of the road unless signs say otherwise.

question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When no other cars are on the road.,b:Never; always follow the posted limit.,c:Only when a police officer is present.,d:When conditions are less than perfect (e.g., rain, poor visibility)
note: Reduce speed below the posted limit when the road, weather, visibility, or traffic conditions make the posted speed unsafe.

question: Faced with an oncoming car on your left and a bicyclist on your right, you should:
options: a:Pull onto the shoulder.,b:Split the difference.,c:Let the car pass and then pass the bicyclist.
note: Avoid trying to deal with two hazards at once; let the oncoming car pass first, then safely pass the bicyclist when there is adequate room.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to stop your vehicle:
options: a:At an intersection with a stop sign.,b:When a traffic officer orders you to stop.,c:Where there is a red light.,d:In all of the above situations
note: Stop at stop signs, red lights, flashing red signals, or whenever a traffic officer directs you to stop.

question: If a green arrow changes to a steady green, what must you do when turning?
options: a:You no longer may turn at all.,b:You have the absolute right-of-way to turn.,c:Stop and wait for the arrow to return,d:You may still turn but must yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.
note: When a green arrow becomes a steady green, turns are still allowed but drivers must yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

question: Large vehicles such as trucks and buses tend to have:
options: a:No blind spots.,b:Smaller blind spots.,c:Larger blind spots.
note: The larger the vehicle, the larger the blind spots around it; be cautious when driving near large vehicles.

question: What is a safe approach to driving through a curve?
options: a:Slow down entering the curve, then gradually accelerate on exit.,b:Maintain a constant speed throughout regardless,c:Accelerate as you enter and slow on exit,d:Brake hard in the center of the curve
note: Reduce speed before entering a curve and gently increase speed as you exit to maintain control.

question: A flashing red light at an intersection requires drivers to:
options: a:Stop only if other vehicles are present.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop, yield, and then proceed when safe (same as a stop sign).,d:Treat it like a flashing yellow signal.
note: A flashing red signal has the same requirement as a stop sign: stop, yield, then proceed when clear.

question: If your vehicle's turn signals stop working, you should indicate turns by using:
options: a:Your headlights,b:Your horn,c:Hand signals
note: When turn signals fail, use the proper hand signals to show your intentions to other drivers.

question: Seat belts are most effective when worn by:
options: a:Passengers when they are on a long drive.,b:The person driving the car.,c:All occupants of a vehicle.
note: Everyone in the vehicle should wear a seat belt, as unbelted occupants become projectiles in a crash and endanger others.

question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, which document must the driver produce?
options: a:Proof of registration,b:Their driver license,c:Proof of insurance
note: When stopped, drivers must present their driver license, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance if requested by an officer.

question: If you need to stop quickly and do not have ABS, you should:
options: a:Firmly pump the brakes while steering to avoid losing control.,b:Hold down the brake pedal at full force without modulation.,c:Lightly tap the brakes repeatedly.,d:Shift into neutral and coast to a stop.
note: Pumping the brakes (rapid, firm pumps) helps maintain steering control and can shorten stopping distance in non-ABS vehicles.

question: When is parking on the shoulder of a freeway allowed?
options: a:Only in an emergency; otherwise it is prohibited.,b:Whenever you want if you turn on hazard flashers.,c:If no part of your vehicle is on the road,d:To check a map or make a quick stop
note: Parking on a freeway shoulder is prohibited except for an emergency; do not stop for non-emergencies on the shoulder.

question: In foggy conditions, what are correct driving practices?
options: a:Drive cautiously, reduce speed, and use low beam headlights.,b:Use high beams to see farther ahead.,c:Stop in the travel lane with parking lights on.,d:Follow closely behind the vehicle ahead
note: Fog reduces visibility; drive slowly, use low beams (high beams reflect back and worsen visibility), and be prepared to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer is directing traffic at a signalized intersection, what should drivers follow?
options: a:Ignore both and proceed with caution,b:Always obey the traffic signal over the officer.,c:Honk to get the officer's attention,d:Follow the officer's directions instead of the traffic lights.
note: An officer's directions take precedence over traffic signals; obey the officer to ensure safety and order.

question: What is the only reliable way to reduce your BAC?
options: a:Drink strong coffee.,b:Exercise vigorously.,c:Allow your body time to metabolize the alcohol.,d:Take a cold shower.
note: Only time allows your body to eliminate alcohol and reduce BAC; coffee, showers, or exercise do not lower BAC.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:The larger vehicle,b:The car on the right,c:The car on the left
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right and allow them to proceed.

question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:
options: a:Allow the motorcycle to use only half of a lane.,b:Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.,c:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a traffic lane; do not crowd them or share a lane.

question: What color are guide signs that provide directional and mileage information?
options: a:Green,b:Yellow,c:Red,d:Blue
note: Guide signs (destination signs) are green and give directions and distances to locations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Early enough so other drivers know your intention in advance.,b:Just as you start to change lanes,c:Only after you begin passing,d:Not necessary if you have a clear view
note: Signal early to give other drivers sufficient notice of your intention to pass or change lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing on a two-way, two-lane road, you must:
options: a:Be able to return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.,b:Pass as quickly as possible regardless of visibility.,c:Use the shoulder to pass when necessary.
note: You may only pass if you can see clearly ahead, can return to your lane before encountering oncoming traffic, and it is legal and safe to do so.

question: To relieve fatigue on a long trip, it's a good idea to:
options: a:Stop for a short rest every two hours.,b:Only drink caffeinated beverages and continue driving.,c:Drive without breaks until the destination.,d:Keep windows closed at all times.
note: Stopping every couple of hours for a short break helps avoid fatigue; nap or rest if drowsy.

question: What do downward-facing triangular traffic signs usually indicate?
options: a:School zones,b:Yield signs,c:Construction zones
note: A downward-pointing triangle indicates a yield sign; yield to other traffic or pedestrians when you see this sign.

question: Turning your head to check a blind spot before changing lanes is:
options: a:Unnecessary if you have mirrors.,b:A good driving habit.,c:A bad driving habit.
note: Physically checking blind spots by glancing over your shoulder is essential when changing lanes because mirrors do not show everything.

question: If another driver is trying to pass you, you should:
options: a:Brake sharply to discourage them.,b:Pull completely off the road.,c:Speed up to block the pass.,d:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow the pass to be completed safely.
note: Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed so the passing driver can move back into the lane safely.

question: What is the “No zone” in relation to large trucks and buses?
options: a:An area where civilians may not pull over.,b:A reduced speed area near trucks.,c:A zone with special parking restrictions.,d:Blind spots around a truck or bus where cars may be hidden.
note: Large trucks and buses have blind spots on the front, both sides, and the rear called “No zones” where smaller vehicles may be unseen.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, what is the proper response?
options: a:Brake hard immediately.,b:Ease off the gas, steer straight, and slow gradually.,c:Maintain your speed and hold the wheel loosely
note: If a tire blows, hold the steering wheel firmly, keep the vehicle straight, ease off the accelerator, do not brake until the vehicle is under control, then pull off the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While in a travel lane, which actions are prohibited?
options: a:Stopping to drop off passengers.,b:Making a U-turn when you missed your freeway entrance.,c:Stopping to look up an address.
note: You should not stop in a travel lane for any reason. If you miss an exit, continue to the next safe place to turn around; do not back up or stop in the lane.

question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a:When directed by a flagger or stop sign or when flashing red signals and gates are operating.,b:Only when you see a train approaching.,c:Only if other cars are stopped at the crossing.
note: Stop at a railroad crossing when instructed by a flagger, stop sign, or active warning devices such as flashing red lights or lowered gates.

question: If a vehicle equipped with ABS (Anti-Lock Braking System) starts to lose traction on a slippery surface, what should you do?
options: a:Pump the brakes rapidly.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal and steer out of danger.,c:Press the accelerator to regain traction.,d:Release the brake and then reapply.
note: If your vehicle has ABS and you lose traction, press hard on the brake pedal and hold it; the system will pulse the brakes automatically while you steer to safety. Pumping or releasing the brake may disengage ABS and reduce braking effectiveness.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal turns green, you should:
options: a:Accelerate as quickly as possible.,b:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.,c:Back up slowly.
note: A green light permits you to go but you must yield to pedestrians and any vehicles still in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a Merging Traffic sign on the freeway, what is appropriate?
options: a:Always remain at your present speed.,b:Make room for entering vehicles, moving over a lane if possible.,c:Honk at incoming traffic to warn them.
note: On multi-lane roads, make room for merging vehicles by moving over a lane if it is clear and safe to do so.

question: What's the best response when someone is tailgating you?
options: a:Slam on your brakes to scare them off.,b:Change lanes or gradually slow so they can pass.,c:Speed up to increase the distance between you and the tailgater.
note: To reduce rear-end crash risk, slow gradually or change lanes to let the tailgater pass; do not brake-check or speed up aggressively.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers?
options: a:Only when they are on your left and you arrived first,b:When entering a street from a garage, alley, or driveway.,c:Never yield when you have the right-of-way,d:When your traffic signal is a green arrow
note: Vehicles entering from driveways, alleys, or garages must yield to traffic and pedestrians on the roadway.

question: A properly adjusted seat belt should:
options: a:Be loose enough to slide easily.,b:Be buckled snugly across your hip bones and the lower abdomen with the shoulder belt across the chest.,c:Be worn under the arm for comfort.,d:Only be used for long trips.
note: Lap belts should fit snugly across the hips and shoulder belts across the chest to provide proper protection.

question: Which factor greatly affects your ability to stop a vehicle?
options: a:The road condition and surface traction,b:The color of your vehicle,c:The type of music played,d:Time of day only
note: Stopping distance depends on road condition (wet, icy, gravel) as well as perception and reaction time and braking capability.

question: An octagonal sign always means:
options: a:Hospital ahead.,b:Stop.,c:Speed limit.
note: A red eight-sided (octagonal) sign indicates you must come to a complete stop at the marked stop line or before entering the intersection.

question: An orange-colored road sign indicates:
options: a:The start of a no passing zone.,b:A school zone is ahead.,c:Construction, maintenance, or emergency operations ahead.
note: Orange signs warn of construction, maintenance, or emergency operations and should prompt slower speeds and extra caution.

question: Which statement is true about alcohol's effects?
options: a:Even the smallest amount of alcohol can impair concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.,b:Only BAC above the legal limit affects driving.,c:Alcohol does not affect driving ability.,d:You can safely mix alcohol with some medications.
note: Any alcohol can impair crucial mental functions for driving; no amount is guaranteed safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, what steps should you take?
options: a:Check mirrors and blind spots, signal, and re-enter the lane when you can see the passed vehicle's front in your mirror.,b:Honk your horn at least three times.,c:Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
note: Before passing, signal, check mirrors and blind spots, pass safely, then return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle's front in your rearview mirror.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing where you don't see or hear a train, when must you stop?
options: a:Only when a train is visible.,b:You never have to stop if you don't see a train.,c:If flashing lights are activated, a gate is lowered, or a stop sign is posted.,d:Only if someone signals you to stop.
note: Stop when lights flash, gates are down, a stop sign is present, a flagger signals, or a train is visible or close enough to be hazardous.

question: Which commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Always weather-related issues.,b:Only vehicle failures.,c:Proper use of turn signals.,d:Inattentive driving, excessive speed for conditions, and following too closely.
note: Inattention, inappropriate speed for conditions, and tailgating are frequent contributors to crashes.
